Take with water at bedtime, at least 1 hour after the evening meal

summary: Thalidomide is an immunomodulatory agent (IMiD) used with dexamethasone for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma and for the cutaneous manifestations of moderate-to-severe erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL). It is a potent human teratogen: even a single dose during pregnancy can cause severe, often fatal birth defects (phocomelia/amelia), so it carries a boxed warning and is available only through the restricted THALOMID REMS program. It also markedly increases venous thromboembolism risk, especially with dexamethasone.
indications: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, in combination with dexamethasone
Acute treatment of the cutaneous manifestations of moderate to severe erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL)
Maintenance therapy for prevention and suppression of cutaneous ENL recurrence

dosage.d: 200 mg once daily orally with water (dexamethasone 40 mg/day on days 1-4, 9-12, 17-20)
dosage.n: 28-day cycles; take at least 1 hour after the evening meal

dosage.d: 100-300 mg/day once daily; up to 400 mg/day for severe ENL
dosage.t: Once daily (or divided in severe disease)
dosage.n: Start <50 kg patients at low end; continue until reaction subsides (usually >=2 weeks)

dosage.d: Taper in 50 mg decrements every 2-4 weeks; maintain on minimum effective dose
dosage.n: Attempt taper every 3-6 months; concomitant corticosteroids if moderate-severe neuritis

admin: Prescribe and dispense ONLY through the THALOMID REMS program (certified prescribers and pharmacies)
Take once daily with water, preferably at bedtime and at least 1 hour after the evening meal
Do NOT open or crush capsules; if powder contacts skin, wash immediately with soap and water; flush mucous membranes with water
Confirm negative pregnancy test before starting and continue testing per REMS in females of reproductive potential
Interrupt dosing for constipation, somnolence, or peripheral neuropathy and consider a reduced dose on resumption
moa: The mechanism is not fully understood. Thalidomide binds cereblon, a component of an E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, and has immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and antiangiogenic properties. Effects include suppression of excessive TNF-alpha production, down-modulation of leukocyte adhesion molecules, modulation of IL-10/IL-12, increased circulating natural killer cells with IL-2 and interferon-gamma in myeloma, and inhibition of angiogenesis.

absolute: Pregnancy - potent human teratogen (boxed warning); never use in females who are or could become pregnant
Demonstrated hypersensitivity to thalidomide or any component
relative: Females of reproductive potential not using two reliable contraception methods
History of venous thromboembolism or significant thrombotic risk factors
monitor: Signs/symptoms of DVT and pulmonary embolism

preg: CONTRAINDICATED. Thalidomide is a powerful human teratogen that causes a high frequency of severe and life-threatening birth defects (amelia, phocomelia, hypoplastic/absent bones, external ear abnormalities, facial palsy, eye abnormalities, congenital heart defects, alimentary/urinary/genital malformations), with mortality at or shortly after birth in about 40% of affected infants. Even a single dose can cause severe birth defects. Pregnancy must be excluded before and prevented during therapy using two reliable contraception methods (per the THALOMID REMS program). Discontinue immediately if pregnancy occurs and report exposure to the FDA MedWatch and REMS Call Center.
lact: It is not known whether thalidomide is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a nursing infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment has been established for renal impairment; thalidomide is minimally renally excreted as unchanged drug. Use with caution and monitor; hemodialysis patients have specific timing considerations in myeloma protocols.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment has been established for hepatic impairment; use with caution.

major: Other thrombogenic agents (e.g., erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, estrogen-containing therapies, dexamethasone) - markedly increased venous thromboembolism risk
Pembrolizumab added to a thalidomide analogue plus dexamethasone - increased mortality in multiple myeloma (not recommended)
moderate: CNS depressants (opioids, antihistamines, antipsychotics, anxiolytics, alcohol) - additive sedation; avoid
Drugs causing peripheral neuropathy (bortezomib, cisplatin, vincristine, paclitaxel, metronidazole, etc.) - additive neuropathy
Drugs causing bradycardia (beta-blockers, calcium-channel blockers, digoxin, lithium) - additive bradycardia
minor: Drugs that reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy (rifampin, certain HIV protease inhibitors, griseofulvin, modafinil) - require additional contraception
interactions.food: Take at least 1 hour after the evening meal; no major clinical food interaction otherwise
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - additive CNS depression and additive peripheral neuropathy
interactions.diagnostics: May increase HIV viral load in HIV-seropositive patients; monitor blood counts and calcium

serious: Venous and arterial thromboembolism (DVT, pulmonary embolism, MI, stroke) - boxed warning
Severe cutaneous reactions (including Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis / DRESS)
emergency: Embryo-fetal exposure (any pregnancy during therapy) - medical emergency
Signs of pulmonary embolism (sudden dyspnea, chest pain) or stroke/MI

monitoring: Pregnancy testing before and during therapy per THALOMID REMS (females of reproductive potential)
Signs and symptoms of thromboembolism (leg swelling, chest pain, dyspnea)
Periodic neurologic exam for peripheral neuropathy
counsel: This drug causes severe birth defects even from a single dose - it must NEVER be taken if you are or could become pregnant; females must use two reliable forms of contraception and males must use condoms as required by the REMS program
Do not donate blood or sperm during treatment and for the required period afterward
Do not share this medication; do not open or crush the capsules; wash skin immediately if powder contacts it
Seek urgent care for leg swelling/pain, chest pain, or shortness of breath (clot/embolism), or for numbness/tingling in hands or feet (nerve damage)
Avoid alcohol and other sedating drugs; take at bedtime as it causes drowsiness; rise slowly to avoid dizziness
pk: Slowly absorbed; sedative effect within hours of a dose
Plasma peak approximately 2.9 to 5.7 hours after an oral dose
Mean terminal half-life approximately 5 to 7 hours
Once-daily dosing; effects on inflammation/disease accrue over days to weeks
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect from light; do not repackage (REMS)
pearls: BOXED WARNING: potent teratogen (phocomelia/amelia) - a single capsule can cause severe birth defects; available only via the restricted THALOMID REMS program
BOXED WARNING: significantly increased venous thromboembolism (DVT/PE), especially combined with dexamethasone - consider thromboprophylaxis based on individual risk
Peripheral neuropathy can be dose-limiting and may be irreversible - monitor and interrupt/reduce dose
Historically the agent responsible for the 1950s-60s birth-defect tragedy; modern use is tightly REMS-controlled
missed: If you miss a dose and it is within about 12 hours of the usual time, take it; if more than 12 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and resume the normal schedule. Do not take two doses at once. Never alter your contraception requirements because of a missed dose.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. In overdose, monitor vital signs and provide supportive care to maintain blood pressure and respiratory status. Manage excessive sedation supportively.
